operations.description:
Search and list timelogs with filtering, pagination, and sorting capabilities.

This operation retrieves timelogs matching specified search criteria including date range, project, task, billable status, and employee filters. Results are returned in paginated format optimized for list displays. Timelogs are strictly isolated per organization - users only see timelogs within their current organization context.

Timelogs can be filtered by date range to view entries within specific periods, by project to see all time logged against a particular project, by task to view time spent on specific tasks, or by billable status to separate billable from non-billable time. These filtering capabilities support reporting and analysis of time data.

Employees can only see their own timelogs unless they have time management permissions. Users with time management permission can view all timelogs within their organization.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_timelogs table with pagination and filtering based on request body criteria.

Filtering rules:
- Apply date range filter on date field (from_date and to_date)
- Filter by hrm_time_track_project_id if project_id provided
- Filter by hrm_time_track_task_id if task_id provided
- Filter by billable status if billable flag provided
- Filter by hrm_time_track_employee_id if employee_id provided
- Always filter by current organization context (hrm_time_track_organization_id)
- Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL) unless explicitly requested

Join operations:
- Left join with hrm_time_track_projects to include project name and status
- Left join with hrm_time_track_tasks to include task name when task_id is present
- Left join with hrm_time_track_employees to include employee name
- Left join with hrm_time_track_timesheets to determine timesheet status (for editability)

Sorting:
- Default sort by date descending
- Support custom sorting on date, duration_seconds, project_id, employee_id

Pagination:
- Use cursor-based pagination for large result sets
- Return total count, page size, and cursor tokens

Authorization:
- Verify user belongs to the organization context
- Employees can only see their own timelogs by default
- Users with time management permission can see all organization timelogs

Edge cases:
- Return empty result set if no timelogs match criteria
- Handle null task_id gracefully (timelogs without task assignment)
- Ensure date filtering uses proper timezone handling

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timelog summary records optimized for administrative list displays with project, task, and employee information.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including date range filters, project, task, employee, billable status filters, pagination parameters, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single timelog record by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete timelog details including the associated employee, project, and optional task information. Timelogs contain date, duration in seconds, billable status, and optional notes describing the work performed.

Authorization: Employees can only view their own timelogs. Users with time:view_all permission can view any timelog within their organization. All timelog data is strictly isolated per organization.

Error Handling: Returns 404 if the timelog does not exist or has been soft deleted. Returns 403 if the requesting user lacks permission to view the timelog.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_timelogs table for the record matching the provided timelogId.

Verify the timelog exists and is not soft deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).

Perform authorization check:
- If requesting user is an employee, verify hrm_time_track_employee_id matches the user's employee record
- If requesting user has time:view_all permission, allow access to any timelog in their organization
- Verify the timelog's organization matches the user's current organization context

Join with related tables to include employee, project, and task data in the response.

Return the full timelog entity with all fields and relationships.

Handle edge cases:
- Return 404 for non-existent or soft-deleted timelogs
- Return 403 for unauthorized access attempts
- Ensure organization isolation is enforced

responseBody.description: Complete timelog record including employee, project, and task relationships.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timelog to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Create a new timelog entry to record work time performed by the authenticated employee.

This operation allows employees to log time spent on projects and tasks within their organization. Each timelog captures the date of work, duration in seconds, project assignment, optional task assignment, billable status, and optional notes describing the work performed.

Timelogs are owned by the employee who creates them and cannot be created on behalf of other employees. All timelogs are strictly isolated within the organization context, ensuring data separation between organizations.

Timelogs form the foundation for timesheet creation and approval workflows. Once created, timelogs can be included in weekly timesheets for submission and approval. Timelogs can be filtered by date range, project, task, and billable status for reporting purposes.

Required fields include the work date, duration, project assignment, and billable status. Task assignment is optional for general project work without specific task tracking.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into hrm_time_track_timelogs table.

Authentication Context:
- Extract employee_id from authenticated user's current organization membership
- Extract organization_id from authenticated user's selected organization context
- Validate user has permission to create timelogs in this organization

Validation:
- Verify hrm_time_track_project_id exists and belongs to the same organization
- If hrm_time_track_task_id is provided, verify it exists and belongs to the same project
- Validate date is not in the future (allow reasonable tolerance for timezone differences)
- Validate duration_seconds is positive and within reasonable bounds (e.g., 1 second to 24 hours)
- Ensure employee can only create timelogs for themselves (ownership rule)

Database Operation:
- Insert new timelog with provided fields
- System automatically generates: id (UUID), created_at (current timestamp), updated_at (current timestamp)
- deleted_at remains null for active records

Post-Creation:
- Record activity log entry for audit trail
- Return the created timelog with all fields populated

Error Handling:
- Return 400 Bad Request for validation failures (invalid date, duration, project/task references)
- Return 403 Forbidden if user attempts to create timelog for another employee
- Return 404 Not Found if referenced project or task doesn't exist
- Return 403 Forbidden if project/task belongs to different organization

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog with all fields populated including system-generated identifiers and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Timelog creation data including work date, duration, project assignment, optional task, billable status, and notes.

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog record with new date, duration, project, task, notes, or billable status.

This operation allows modification of timelog details including work date, duration in seconds, project assignment, optional task assignment, billable flag, and descriptive notes. The timelog must exist and belong to the requesting employee's organization.

Permission Requirements:
- Employees can update only their own timelogs that are not part of an approved timesheet
- Users with time management permission can update any employee's timelogs regardless of timesheet status
- Timelogs in approved timesheets are locked and cannot be modified by regular employees

Error Handling:
- Returns 404 if timelog does not exist or belongs to a different organization
- Returns 403 if employee attempts to update another employee's timelog
- Returns 403 if employee attempts to update a timelog in an approved timesheet
- Returns validation errors if updated project is archived or completed (blocks new timelog associations)
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_timelogs table for the timelog by id, including joins to verify organization context.

1. Verify timelog exists and belongs to the current organization context
2. Check if timelog is associated with any timesheet via hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs junction table
3. If timelog is in a timesheet with status 'approved', reject the update unless user has time management permission
4. Verify employee ownership: requesting employee must match hrm_time_track_employee_id unless user has time management permission
5. Validate new project status: if project_id is updated, verify the target project status is 'active' (not archived or completed)
6. Update allowed fields: date, duration_seconds, hrm_time_track_project_id, hrm_time_track_task_id, billable, notes
7. DO NOT allow updates to: id, hrm_time_track_employee_id, hrm_time_track_organization_id, created_at, deleted_at
8. Set updated_at to current timestamp
9. Record activity log entry in hrm_time_track_activity_logs with action type, user, organization, and change details
10. Return the updated timelog entity with all fields including relationships

Edge Cases:
- If task_id is set to null, remove task association but keep project
- If project_id changes, task_id should be validated to belong to the new project or set to null
- Duration must be positive (greater than 0 seconds)
- Date must be a valid datetime value

responseBody.description: Updated timelog record with all fields including employee, project, and task relationships.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timelog to update (global scope)
parameters.name: timelogId

requestBody.description: Timelog update data including date, duration, project, task, billable status, and optional notes. Employee and organization fields cannot be modified.

operations.description:
Delete a timelog entry by ID.

This operation removes a time entry from the system. Deletion is subject to strict business rules based on timesheet status and user permissions. Employees can only delete their own timelogs that are not included in any submitted or approved timesheet. Users with time management permissions can delete any timelog regardless of timesheet status.

When a timelog is part of a submitted or approved timesheet, deletion is blocked to maintain timesheet integrity. If a timesheet is rejected and returns to draft status, the associated timelogs become deletable again.

The deletion action is recorded in the activity log for audit purposes. Timelogs are permanently removed when their organization is deleted.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Extract timelogId from path parameter and validate UUID format.
2. Fetch the timelog record by ID, including employee, project, and task relationships.
3. Verify the timelog exists and belongs to the current organization context.
4. Check if the timelog is associated with any timesheet by querying hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs junction table.
5. If associated with a timesheet, check the timesheet status:
   - If status is 'submitted' or 'approved', block deletion and return 403 Forbidden.
   - If status is 'draft' or 'rejected', allow deletion to proceed.
6. Verify user authorization:
   - If user is the timelog owner (employee match), allow deletion if timesheet check passes.
   - If user has 'time management' permission, allow deletion regardless of ownership.
   - Otherwise, return 403 Forbidden.
7. Delete the timelog record from hrm_time_track_timelogs table.
8. Record the deletion action in hrm_time_track_activity_logs with action type, user, timestamp, and affected resource.
9. Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timelog to delete (UUID format).
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Search and list timesheets with filtering by status and date range.

This endpoint enables employees to browse their timesheets with support for status filtering (draft, submitted, approved, rejected) and date range queries. Employees can only view their own timesheets, while users with time:approve permission can view all submitted timesheets within their organization.

Timesheets are returned in paginated format with cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large result sets. The response includes summary information optimized for list displays, including week dates, status, and total hours.

Rejected timesheets are returned to draft status for modification and resubmission. Approved timesheets have locked timelogs that cannot be edited or deleted.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_timesheets table with pagination and filtering based on request body criteria.

Authorization: Verify the requesting user's access level. Employees can only query timesheets where hrm_time_track_employee_id matches their employee record. Users with time:approve permission can query all timesheets within their organization context.

Filtering: Apply status filter from request body (draft, submitted, approved, rejected). Apply date range filter on week_start_date and week_end_date fields. Support filtering by employee ID for administrative views.

Join: Left join with hrm_time_track_employees to include employee name and department information. Left join with hrm_time_track_members (approver) to include approver name when status is approved.

Aggregation: Calculate total_hours by summing duration_seconds from related hrm_time_track_timelogs (where timelog deleted_at is null and timelog date falls within week_start_date to week_end_date).

Pagination: Implement cursor-based pagination using week_start_date and id as composite cursor. Return pagination metadata including has_next, has_previous, and cursor values.

Sorting: Default sort by week_start_date descending (newest first). Support custom sorting on week_start_date, status, or total_hours.

Exclusions: Filter out timesheets where deleted_at is not null. Only return active timesheets.

Response transformation: Map database fields to IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.ISummary DTO. Include id, status, week_start_date, week_end_date, total_hours, employee information, and approver information (when approved).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summary records with week dates, status, total hours, and employee information optimized for list displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for timesheets including status filter, date range, employee filter, pagination parameters, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timesheet by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete timesheet details including the associated employee, approval status, week period, and approval metadata. Timesheets represent weekly collections of timelogs organized from Monday to Sunday for employee time tracking and approval workflows.

Access Control: Employees can view their own timesheets. Users with time:approve permission can view all timesheets within their organization. The system enforces organization-level data isolation.

Status Information: The response includes the current approval status (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected), approval timestamp and approver details if approved, and rejection reason if rejected.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_track_timesheets table for a single record matching the provided timesheetId UUID.

Authorization: Verify the requesting user has permission to view this timesheet. Employees can only view their own timesheets (where hrm_time_track_employee_id matches their employee record). Users with time:approve permission can view any timesheet in their organization.

Query: SELECT * FROM hrm_time_track_timesheets WHERE id = {timesheetId} AND deleted_at IS NULL.

Join: Include employee information via left join with hrm_time_track_employees on hrm_time_track_employee_id. Include approver member information via left join with hrm_time_track_members on hrm_time_track_member_id when present.

Error handling: Return 404 Not Found if no timesheet matches the ID or if the timesheet is soft-deleted. Return 403 Forbidden if the user lacks permission to view this timesheet.

Return the complete timesheet entity with all fields including nested employee and approver references.

responseBody.description: Complete timesheet entity including employee reference, approval status, week dates, and approval metadata.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to retrieve (UUID format).
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Creates a new draft timesheet for an employee covering a specific week period.

This operation allows employees to create a timesheet for a given week (Monday to Sunday). The timesheet is created in draft status and automatically includes all timelogs that the employee has logged during that week period. The week is identified by its start date (Monday), and the end date (Sunday) is calculated automatically.

A timesheet can only be created if no existing timesheet (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected) exists for the same employee and week. This ensures one timesheet per employee per week. The created timesheet can be modified by the employee until it is submitted for approval.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new timesheet record in hrm_time_track_timesheets table with the following logic:

1. Validate that the authenticated user has an employee record in the organization context.
2. Extract week_start_date from request body and calculate week_end_date (Sunday, 6 days after Monday).
3. Check for existing timesheet with same hrm_time_track_employee_id and week_start_date combination (unique constraint).
4. If exists, return 409 Conflict error.
5. Create timesheet record with:
   - hrm_time_track_employee_id: from authenticated user's employee record
   - status: 'draft'
   - week_start_date: from request (normalized to start of day)
   - week_end_date: calculated (week_start_date + 6 days, end of day)
   - created_at, updated_at: current timestamp
   - hrm_time_track_member_id, approved_at, rejected_at, rejection_reason: null
6. The timesheet automatically includes all timelogs from hrm_time_track_timelogs where:
   - hrm_time_track_employee_id matches the timesheet's employee
   - date falls between week_start_date and week_end_date (inclusive)
7. Return the created timesheet entity with full details.

Error handling:
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid date format, week_start_date not on Monday
- 409 Conflict: Timesheet already exists for this employee and week
- 403 Forbidden: User not authorized or not an employee in the organization

responseBody.description: The newly created timesheet entity in draft status, including week dates, status, and employee reference.

requestBody.description: Timesheet creation request containing the week start date (Monday) for the new timesheet. The week end date will be automatically calculated as Sunday (6 days after the start date).

operations.description:
Updates a timesheet's properties, primarily managing status transitions in the approval workflow.

This operation allows employees to submit draft timesheets for approval, administrators to approve or reject submitted timesheets, and employees to modify rejected timesheets back to draft status. The operation enforces strict status transition rules and validates that approved timesheets cannot be modified. When rejecting a timesheet, a rejection reason must be provided to inform the employee of issues to address before resubmission.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate timesheet exists and retrieve current record from hrm_time_track_timesheets table by id.

2. Check authorization: verify requesting user has permission to modify this timesheet (employee owner or time management permission).

3. Validate status transition rules:
   - draft → submitted: allowed for employee owner
   - submitted → approved: allowed for users with time:approve permission
   - submitted → rejected: allowed for users with time:approve permission, requires rejection_reason
   - rejected → draft: allowed for employee owner
   - approved → any: NOT ALLOWED (approved timesheets are locked)
   - Any other transitions: NOT ALLOWED

4. If status is transitioning to 'submitted':
   - Verify timesheet has at least one timelog (join with hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs)
   - Verify no other timesheet for same employee and week exists with status 'submitted' or 'approved' (check unique constraint)

5. If status is transitioning to 'approved':
   - Set approved_at to current timestamp
   - Set hrm_time_track_member_id to approver's member id
   - Lock all associated timelogs from editing

6. If status is transitioning to 'rejected':
   - Validate rejection_reason is provided and not empty
   - Set rejected_at to current timestamp
   - Timesheet automatically returns to 'draft' status for employee modification

7. Update the timesheet record with validated changes.

8. Record activity log entry for audit trail.

9. Return updated timesheet entity.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet entity with all current properties including status, dates, and approval information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to update (global scope).
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Timesheet update data including status transition and optional rejection reason when rejecting a submitted timesheet.

operations.description:
Delete a timesheet by ID.

This operation removes a timesheet from the system. Deletion permissions depend on the user's role and the timesheet's current status. Employees can only delete their own timesheets that are in draft status. Users with time management permissions can delete any timesheet regardless of status or ownership.

Timesheets in submitted, approved, or rejected status are protected from deletion by regular employees to maintain the integrity of the approval workflow. Only authorized administrators can remove timesheets that have progressed beyond draft status.

The deletion is performed as a soft delete, preserving the timesheet record in the database while marking it as deleted. This maintains referential integrity and enables audit trail capabilities.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a timesheet by ID with authorization validation.

Authorization checks:
1. Verify the authenticated user is either:
   - The employee who owns the timesheet AND the timesheet status is 'draft'
   - A user with time:management permission (can delete any timesheet regardless of status)

Validation rules:
- Reject deletion if employee attempts to delete another employee's timesheet
- Reject deletion if employee attempts to delete a timesheet with status 'submitted', 'approved', or 'rejected'
- Users with time:management permission bypass status restrictions

Implementation steps:
1. Fetch the timesheet by ID, including employee relationship
2. Verify authorization based on rules above
3. Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp
4. If user has time:management permission, record deletion in activity log
5. Return 204 No Content on success

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found if timesheet doesn't exist
- 403 Forbidden if unauthorized deletion attempt
- 409 Conflict if timesheet is part of approved workflow (for non-admin users)

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to delete (global scope).
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created before it can be deleted. The timesheetId path parameter references a timesheet that was previously created via this POST operation.

operations.description:
Update the timelog associations for a specific timesheet by adding or removing timelogs.

This operation allows employees to modify which timelogs are included in their draft timesheets. Timelogs can be added to include additional work entries or removed to exclude entries from the weekly submission. The operation validates that the timesheet is in draft status, as only draft timesheets can be modified. Once a timesheet is submitted or approved, timelog associations become locked and cannot be changed through this endpoint.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate the timesheet exists and is not soft-deleted.
2. Verify the timesheet status is 'draft' - reject if submitted, approved, or rejected.
3. Verify the authenticated employee owns the timesheet (hrm_time_track_employee_id matches).
4. For timelogs to add:
   - Validate each timelog exists and is not soft-deleted.
   - Verify each timelog belongs to the same employee as the timesheet.
   - Verify each timelog's date falls within the timesheet's week range (week_start_date to week_end_date).
   - Check if timelog is already associated with this timesheet - skip if already present.
   - Create new records in hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs junction table.
5. For timelogs to remove:
   - Validate the association exists in hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs.
   - Delete the association records from the junction table.
6. Recalculate and update the timesheet's total hours based on included timelogs.
7. Update the timesheet's updated_at timestamp.
8. Return the updated timesheet with its associated timelogs.
9. Handle edge cases: empty add/remove arrays, duplicate timelog IDs in request, timelogs outside week range.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet record with its associated timelogs after the modification.

parameters.description: UUID of the timesheet whose timelog associations are being updated.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Timelog association update request containing arrays of timelog IDs to add to or remove from the timesheet.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timelog association within a timesheet by its unique identifier.

This operation returns detailed information about a single timelog entry that is explicitly included in a weekly timesheet for approval processing. The response includes the association metadata (when the timelog was added to the timesheet) along with the complete timelog details (date, duration, project, task, billable status, and notes).

Access control requires the requesting user to have appropriate permissions to view the timesheet and its associated timelogs. Employees can view their own timesheet timelog associations, while users with time management permissions can view all associations within their organization.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs table for the record matching the provided timesheet_id and the specific timesheet-timelog association id.

1. Validate that the timesheet_id exists and belongs to the requesting user's organization
2. Validate that the timesheetTimelogId exists and is associated with the specified timesheet
3. Join with hrm_time_track_timelogs to retrieve complete timelog details
4. Join with hrm_time_track_projects to include project information
5. Optionally join with hrm_time_track_tasks if task_id is present
6. Apply authorization checks: employee can view their own timesheet associations, users with time:view_all permission can view all
7. Return the full entity with all relationships populated
8. Handle cases where the timesheet or timelog has been soft deleted by returning 404

responseBody.description: Complete timesheet-timelog association entity including association metadata and full timelog details with project and task references.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent timesheet that contains this timelog association (global scope)

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet-timelog association record (global scope)

operations.description:
Retrieve the audit trail of status changes for a specific timesheet.

This endpoint returns all snapshot records capturing the timesheet's approval workflow history, including submission, approval, and rejection events. Each snapshot records the status value, the member who performed the action, and the timestamp. Results are returned in paginated format with optional filtering by status.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_timesheets table to verify the timesheet exists and belongs to the requesting member's organization.

Query hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots table filtering by:
- hrm_time_track_timesheet_id = timesheetId (path parameter)
- Optional: status filter from request body

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based pagination from request body.

Sort results by created_at in descending order (most recent first) by default.

Join with hrm_time_track_members to include member information (email, display name) for the action performer.

Return paginated response with snapshot summaries including status, member reference, and created_at timestamp.

Validate that the timesheet exists and is not soft-deleted before returning snapshots.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet snapshot summaries showing status changes in the approval workflow. Each snapshot includes the status value, the member who performed the action, and the timestamp of the change.

parameters.description: UUID of the timesheet to retrieve snapshots for. The timesheet must exist and belong to the requesting member's organization.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Filtering and pagination parameters for timesheet snapshots. Includes optional status filter to narrow results to specific status values (draft, submitted, approved, rejected) and pagination configuration for result set size and cursor.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timesheet snapshot by timesheet ID and snapshot ID.

This operation returns the complete details of a timesheet snapshot, which captures a point-in-time status change during the timesheet approval workflow. Each snapshot records the timesheet status, the member who performed the action, and the exact timestamp of the status change.

Snapshots are immutable audit records that provide compliance and accountability for timesheet status transitions including submission, approval, and rejection events. Organizations can use this data to review the complete approval history and verify who performed each action and when it occurred.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots table for a record matching both the timesheet_id and the snapshot id.

1. Validate that the timesheetId and snapshotId parameters are valid UUIDs.
2. Execute a SELECT query on hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots where id equals snapshotId and hrm_time_track_timesheet_id equals timesheetId.
3. Verify the snapshot exists and belongs to the specified timesheet.
4. Return the complete snapshot record including all fields: id, hrm_time_track_timesheet_id, hrm_time_track_member_id, status, and created_at.
5. If no matching snapshot is found, return a 404 Not Found error.
6. Ensure proper authorization checks verify the requesting user has permission to view timesheet snapshots for the specified timesheet.
7. The snapshot data is read-only and immutable; no modifications are allowed through this endpoint.

responseBody.description: Complete timesheet snapshot record containing the status change details, including the timesheet reference, member who performed the action, status value, and creation timestamp.

parameters.description: UUID of the timesheet to which this snapshot belongs. Identifies the specific timesheet whose status change is captured in this snapshot.
parameters.name: timesheetId

parameters.description: UUID of the specific timesheet snapshot to retrieve. Uniquely identifies the point-in-time status change record within the timesheet's approval history.
parameters.name: snapshotId

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must exist before snapshots can be created for it during status transitions

operations.description:
Search and list timer records with filtering and pagination support.

This operation retrieves timer sessions with optional filters for employee, project, task, and active status. Employees can only view their own timers, while users with administrative permissions can search across all timers within their organization.

The response includes timer details such as start time, associated project and task, description, and current active status. Results are returned in paginated format with cursor-based navigation for large result sets.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_timers table with pagination and filtering based on request body parameters.

Filtering:
- Filter by employee_id (hrm_time_track_employee_id) - required for employee-scoped queries
- Filter by project_id (hrm_time_track_project_id) - optional
- Filter by task_id (hrm_time_track_task_id) - optional
- Filter by is_active status - optional, defaults to showing active timers
- Organization scoping through employee relationship for data isolation

Pagination:
- Support cursor-based pagination with page_token and page_size parameters
- Default page size should be reasonable for list displays (e.g., 20-50 records)
- Return pagination metadata including has_next, has_previous, and next_page_token

Sorting:
- Support sorting by started_at (default descending - newest first)
- Support sorting by employee, project, or task

Authorization:
- Employees can only query their own timers (filter by their employee_id)
- Users with time management or employee management permissions can query all timers within their organization
- Validate organization context matches authenticated user's organization

Response construction:
- Return timer summary with essential fields: id, employee info, project info, task info (if any), started_at, description, is_active
- Calculate elapsed time for active timers (current time - started_at)
- Include related entity summaries (employee name, project name, task title)
- Exclude sensitive or unnecessary fields for list view optimization

Edge cases:
- Handle case where employee has no active timer (return empty result)
- Handle case where timer was recently stopped but record not yet removed
- Ensure soft-deleted timers are excluded from results

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timer summary records optimized for list displays with essential timer information and related entity details.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for timers including employee, project, task filters, active status filter, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timer session by its unique identifier.

This operation allows employees to view the details of a timer session, including the start timestamp, associated project, optional task assignment, and work description. The timer information helps employees track their real-time work sessions and verify the context of time being recorded.

Employees can only view their own timer sessions. The system enforces data isolation to prevent employees from accessing timer information belonging to other employees within the same organization.

The response includes the full timer entity with nested project and task details, providing complete context about the work being tracked.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_track_timers table by the provided timerId (UUID).

Verify authorization: ensure the requesting employee's ID matches the hrm_time_track_employee_id of the retrieved timer. Throw unauthorized error if mismatch.

If the timer record does not exist, return 404 Not Found.

Include nested project data (id, code, name, description) from hrm_time_track_projects.

If task_id is not null, include nested task data (id, code, name, description, status) from hrm_time_track_tasks.

Return the complete timer entity with all fields: id, started_at, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at, and the nested project/task relationships.

Handle edge cases: timer may have been stopped/discarded (is_active = false), but the record should still be retrievable if it exists.

responseBody.description: Complete timer entity including start timestamp, description, active status, and associated project and task information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timer session to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: timerId

operations.description:
Start a new time tracking timer session for the authenticated employee.

This operation creates a live timer session that tracks work time in real-time. The employee must select a project to associate with the timer. Task association and description are optional. The system automatically records the start timestamp when the timer begins.

Only one active timer is allowed per employee at any time. If the employee already has a running timer, the operation will fail with an error. The employee must be assigned to the selected project within their organization.

The timer continues running until the employee explicitly stops it (creating a timelog) or discards it (no timelog created). Timers persist across session boundaries and continue running even if the employee logs out or closes their browser.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract the authenticated employee from the session context (member_id + organization_id).
2. Query hrm_time_track_timers to check if an active timer exists for this employee (is_active = true).
3. If an active timer exists, return 409 Conflict error.
4. Validate that the project_id belongs to the employee's organization.
5. Validate that the employee is assigned to the project via hrm_time_track_project_members.
6. If task_id is provided, validate that the task belongs to the specified project.
7. Create a new timer record in hrm_time_track_timers with:
   - id: generate UUID
   - hrm_time_track_employee_id: from authenticated employee
   - hrm_time_track_project_id: from request body
   - hrm_time_track_task_id: from request body (nullable)
   - started_at: current timestamp (DateTime.now())
   - description: from request body (nullable)
   - is_active: true
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
8. Return the created timer entity with 201 Created status.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: if no authenticated employee in session
- 404 Not Found: if project or task not found
- 409 Conflict: if employee already has an active timer
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: if project doesn't belong to employee's organization or employee is not assigned to project

responseBody.description: The newly created timer session with all attributes including the automatically generated start timestamp and active status.

requestBody.description: Timer creation request containing the project association and optional task and description. Project is required and must belong to the employee's organization. Task is optional but must belong to the specified project if provided.

operations.description:
Update the description, project, or task association of a running timer session.

This operation allows employees to modify the context of their active timer without stopping it. The timer continues running while these attributes are updated, preserving the elapsed time since the timer was started. Only the employee who owns the timer can update it, and the timer must be in an active state.

The following fields can be updated: description (optional work notes), project (required project association), and task (optional task within the project). System-managed fields such as started_at, is_active, created_at, and updated_at cannot be modified through this endpoint.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Retrieve the timer by timerId and verify the requesting employee owns this timer (check hrm_time_track_employee_id matches authenticated employee). Validate that the timer is currently active (is_active = true). If updating project, verify the employee has access to the new project through hrm_time_track_project_members. If updating task, verify the task belongs to the new project (or existing project if project not changed) and the employee has access to it. Update the editable fields: description, hrm_time_track_project_id, and hrm_time_track_task_id. Set updated_at to current timestamp. Return the updated timer entity with all fields including nested project and task information.

responseBody.description: Complete timer entity with updated attributes and associated project and task information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timer session to update (UUID format, global scope).
parameters.name: timerId

requestBody.description: Editable fields for the timer including optional description, project ID, and optional task ID.

operations.description:
Discards a running timer session without creating a timelog.

This operation terminates an active timer session and does not record any time. Unlike stopping a timer, which creates a timelog with the calculated duration, discarding simply ends the session with no time tracking data preserved. This is useful when an employee starts a timer by mistake or needs to restart time tracking for a different activity.

The employee must be the owner of the timer to discard it. Only one active timer is allowed per employee at any time. After discarding, the employee can start a new timer session if needed.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the timer record by timerId from hrm_time_track_timers table.
2. Verify the timer exists and is currently active (is_active = true).
3. Validate that the authenticated employee (from session) matches the timer's hrm_time_track_employee_id.
4. If ownership validation fails, return 403 Forbidden error.
5. If timer not found, return 404 Not Found error.
6. Delete the timer record from the database.
7. Do NOT create a timelog - discarding means no time is recorded.
8. Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.
9. Handle concurrent modification: if timer was already stopped/discarded, return appropriate error.
10. Log the discard action in activity_logs for audit trail (if required by organization policy).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timer session to discard (global scope).
parameters.name: timerId

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of timer snapshots for a specific timer, showing the complete audit trail of timer lifecycle events.

Timer snapshots capture the state of a timer at key moments: when it starts, when attributes are edited, when it stops, and when it is discarded. This endpoint provides visibility into the complete history of a timer session, enabling compliance tracking and audit requirements.

The response includes snapshot details such as event type, duration, timestamps, and associated entity references (employee, project, task). Results are returned in paginated format with filtering support for event types and date ranges.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots table filtering by hrm_time_track_timer_id from path parameter.

Apply search filters from request body:
- event_type filter (start, stop, discard, edit)
- date range filters on created_at
- pagination parameters (page, pageSize, sortBy, sortOrder)

Join with related tables to include summary data:
- hrm_time_track_employees for employee reference
- hrm_time_track_projects for project reference  
- hrm_time_track_tasks for task reference (nullable)
- hrm_time_track_members for creator reference

Return paginated results with IPageIHrmTimeTrackTimerSnapshot.ISummary type.

Validate that timerId exists and belongs to the requesting employee's organization.

Sort by created_at descending by default to show most recent events first.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timer snapshot summary records showing timer lifecycle events.

parameters.description: UUID of the timer to retrieve snapshots for (global scope)
parameters.name: timerId

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering timer snapshots including event type, date ranges, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific timer snapshot record by its unique identifier.

Timer snapshots are immutable audit trail records that capture the state of a timer at specific lifecycle events (start, stop, discard, edit). Each snapshot provides a complete point-in-time view of the timer including employee, project, task associations, duration, and timestamps. This operation is read-only and returns the full snapshot entity with all denormalized relationship data for comprehensive audit trail visibility.

The snapshot data includes the event type that triggered the snapshot, the duration in seconds at that moment, start and stop timestamps, and any associated work description. All relationship data (employee, project, task) is denormalized into the snapshot to ensure the audit trail remains complete and accurate even if related records are updated or deleted.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots table for a single record matching the provided snapshotId.

Validation:
- Verify the snapshotId exists and is a valid UUID
- Verify the timerId matches the hrm_time_track_timer_id of the snapshot
- Ensure the requesting member has permission to view the timer's employee data

Implementation:
- Perform a SELECT query on hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots WHERE id = snapshotId AND hrm_time_track_timer_id = timerId
- Join with related tables (hrm_time_track_employees, hrm_time_track_projects, hrm_time_track_tasks, hrm_time_track_members) to populate denormalized data if needed
- Return the complete snapshot record with all fields
- Handle case where snapshot not found with 404 response
- Handle case where timerId doesn't match snapshot's timer with 404 response

Security:
- Verify the requesting member has access to the employee who owns the timer
- Ensure organization-level data isolation is enforced
- Only members with appropriate permissions can view timer snapshots

responseBody.description: Complete timer snapshot record containing event type, duration, timestamps, and denormalized employee, project, task, and member information for audit trail purposes.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent timer session that this snapshot belongs to.
parameters.name: timerId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timer snapshot record to retrieve.
parameters.name: snapshotId

operations.description:
List and search activity logs with filtering, sorting, and pagination support.

This endpoint retrieves activity log entries across the organization, allowing administrators and authorized users to audit system events. Activity logs are immutable records that cannot be modified or deleted after creation.

### Filtering and Search

The endpoint supports filtering by:
- Date range (created_at)
- Activity type (employee_created, project_archived, task_status_changed, etc.)
- Organization context (multi-tenancy isolation)
- Associated entities (employee, project, task, timesheet, role, contract, department)

### Sorting and Pagination

Results support server-side sorting by date (newest/oldest first) and cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

### Authorization

Only authenticated members with appropriate audit or admin permissions can access activity logs. Each user can only view logs from organizations they belong to.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_activity_logs table with support for:

1. **Filtering**: Filter by date range, activity_type, organization_id, and optional entity associations (employee_id, project_id, task_id, timesheet_id, role_id, employee_contract_id, department_id)

2. **Sorting**: Order by created_at (descending by default for most recent first)

3. **Pagination**: Implement cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable limit

4. **Multi-tenancy**: Automatically scope results to the requesting user's organizations

5. **Immutability**: Activity logs are read-only; only SELECT queries are performed

6. **Performance**: Leverage existing indexes on hrm_time_track_organization_id, created_at, activity_type, and entity foreign keys for optimal query performance

7. **Error Handling**: Return 403 if user lacks organization membership, 404 if no logs match criteria, 500 for server errors

responseBody.description: Paginated list of activity log entries matching the filter criteria.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for activity logs including date range, activity types, and entity associations.

operations.description:
Retrieves a specific activity log entry by its unique identifier for audit and compliance purposes.

This operation returns the complete details of a single activity log entry including the timestamp, user who performed the action, action type, target entity references, and action metadata. Activity logs provide an immutable audit trail of all significant organizational events such as employee lifecycle changes, project status updates, task modifications, timesheet submissions, and role assignments.

Users must have organization management permission to access activity logs. The returned entry includes all contextual information needed for security auditing, compliance reporting, and transparency purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_track_activity_logs table for a single record matching the provided activityLogId UUID.

1. Validate that the activityLogId is a valid UUID format
2. Verify the requesting user has org:manage permission for the organization owning this activity log
3. Execute SELECT query on hrm_time_track_activity_logs WHERE id = activityLogId
4. Join with related entities (member, employee, project, task, timesheet, role, employeeContract, department) to populate reference data
5. Return the complete activity log entry with all fields
6. Return 404 Not Found if no matching activity log exists
7. Return 403 Forbidden if user lacks organization management permission

responseBody.description: Complete activity log entry including timestamp, action details, user information, and target entity references.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the activity log entry to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: activityLogId

operations.description:
Retrieves the list of organizations available to the currently authenticated user for organization context selection and switching.

This endpoint returns all organizations where the authenticated user has an active membership. Each organization includes the user's assigned role and employee status within that organization, enabling users to understand their access level and current standing in each organization.

The response supports the multi-organization membership workflow, allowing users to view their available organizations and switch between them without logging out. Organization data is strictly isolated — users only see organizations they belong to.
operations.name: available
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_members table to find all organization memberships for the authenticated user ID from the session.

For each membership, join with hrm_time_track_organizations to get organization details (id, name, code, status).

Join with hrm_time_track_employees to retrieve the user's employee record in each organization, including their assigned role (from hrm_time_track_roles) and status.

Filter to only include organizations where the employee status is 'active' or the membership is valid.

Return paginated organization summaries with embedded role information (role name, role type) and employee status.

Order results by organization name alphabetically.

Handle edge cases: user with no organizations returns empty array, user with single organization returns that one organization.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization summaries available to the authenticated user, including organization details and the user's role and status within each organization.

operations.description:
Switch the authenticated user's organization context to a different organization they belong to without logging out.

This operation updates the user's active organization context for all subsequent API requests. The user must be a member of the target organization to perform the switch. After switching, all data access and operations are scoped to the newly selected organization.

The operation validates that the user belongs to the specified organization and has an active employee record within it. If validation succeeds, the session context is updated and the organization details are returned for client confirmation.
operations.name: switchContext
operations.specification:
1. Extract organizationId from path parameter and validate UUID format.
2. Verify the authenticated user has an active session with current organization context.
3. Query hrm_time_track_organizations table to find the target organization by id.
4. Validate the organization exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
5. Verify the authenticated user belongs to the target organization by checking hrm_time_track_members and related employee records.
6. Ensure the user has an active employee record in the target organization (status is not deactivated).
7. Update the user's session context to set the new organization_id.
8. Return the organization details including id, name, description, logo, currency, timezone, and fiscal_start_month.
9. Log the organization switch event in hrm_time_track_activity_logs for audit trail.
10. Handle errors: organization not found, user not a member, organization deleted, or invalid organization ID.

responseBody.description: The organization details of the newly selected organization context, including identity information and operational settings.

parameters.description: The UUID of the organization to switch to. The user must be a member of this organization.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Retrieves the personal dashboard for the authenticated employee within their current organization context.

The dashboard provides a consolidated view of the employee's work activities including active tasks, recent time entries, timesheet status, and project assignments. All data is filtered to show only information relevant to the authenticated employee within their selected organization.

Dashboard content includes task summaries showing open and in-progress tasks with due dates, recent timelog entries for the current week, current timesheet status and submission state, and project membership information. The dashboard updates dynamically based on the employee's current work context and organization selection.

Access is restricted to the employee's own dashboard only. Users with elevated permissions cannot view other employees' personal dashboards as this data is considered private and personal to each employee.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query multiple data sources to assemble the personal dashboard for the authenticated employee:

1. Retrieve the authenticated employee record from the current organization context
2. Fetch active tasks (status: open or in-progress) assigned to the employee, ordered by due date and priority
3. Get recent timelogs for the current week (Monday-Sunday) created by the employee
4. Retrieve the current week's timesheet if it exists, including its status and total hours
5. Fetch project memberships for the employee showing active projects
6. Calculate summary statistics: total active tasks, hours logged this week, pending timesheets

Return all data as a single IHrmTimeTrackPersonalDashboard object. Ensure all queries are scoped to the employee's current organization. Handle cases where no timesheet exists for the current week by returning null for timesheet data. Exclude any data from other organizations even if the user belongs to multiple organizations.

responseBody.description: Personal dashboard data including active tasks, recent timelogs, current timesheet status, project assignments, and summary statistics for the authenticated employee.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of employees for organizational reporting and analysis.

This endpoint provides employee data suitable for administrative dashboards, workforce analysis, and reporting purposes. Users can filter employees by department, employment type, and status using query parameters. The response includes essential employee information such as name, position, role, department, employment type, and status.

Data is isolated by organization - users can only access employee data from their current organization context. The endpoint supports pagination to handle large employee populations efficiently. Filtered results help organizations analyze workforce distribution, track employment types, and monitor employee status across departments.
operations.name: report
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_time_track_employees table with organization scoping based on the current user's context.

Apply filtering based on query parameters:
- Filter by department_id if provided (join with hrm_time_track_departments)
- Filter by employment_type if provided (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern)
- Filter by status if provided (active, deactivated)
- Support text search on position field using trigram index

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based pagination.

Join with related tables for summary data:
- hrm_time_track_members for employee name (via member_id)
- hrm_time_track_departments for department name (via department_id)
- hrm_time_track_roles for role name (via role_id)

Exclude soft-deleted employees (deleted_at IS NULL) unless explicitly requested.

Return paginated response with employee summaries including: id, name, position, role, department, employment_type, status, hire_date.

Enforce organization data isolation - only return employees belonging to the current user's organization.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of employee summaries optimized for reporting and administrative list displays.

operations.description:
Retrieve a hierarchical department report with employee statistics for organizational analysis.

This endpoint returns a structured view of all departments within the organization, showing the parent-child relationships and the number of employees assigned to each department. The report supports organizational analysis by displaying workforce distribution across different business units.

The response includes department identification (id, name, description), hierarchical structure (parent-child relationships), and employee counts for each department. Top-level departments appear at the root level, with child departments nested under their respective parents.

This report is useful for understanding organizational structure, analyzing team sizes, and making management decisions about resource allocation across departments.
operations.name: report
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_departments table to build a hierarchical department report.

1. Fetch all active departments (deleted_at IS NULL) for the current organization from the authenticated user's context.
2. For each department, count the number of active employees (deleted_at IS NULL) assigned to it from hrm_time_track_employees table.
3. Build a hierarchical tree structure by joining departments with their parent departments using parent_department_id.
4. Include department id, name, description, parent_department_id (if exists), and employee_count for each department.
5. Sort departments by name alphabetically within each parent level.
6. Return the hierarchical structure with child departments nested under their parents.

Authorization: Verify the authenticated user belongs to the organization and has permission to view department reports.

Error handling: Return 404 if organization not found, 403 if user lacks permission.

responseBody.description: Hierarchical department report containing department information, parent-child relationships, and employee counts for organizational analysis.

operations.description:
Retrieve role analytics and statistics for the current organization.

This endpoint provides aggregated insights into role distribution, permission assignments, and role usage patterns within the organization. The report includes counts of employees per role, breakdown of permissions across roles, and identification of built-in versus custom roles.

Role reports help administrators understand their permission structure, identify potential role consolidation opportunities, and audit access control configurations. The data is scoped to the currently selected organization and reflects active roles only (excluding soft-deleted roles).
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_time_track_roles table filtered by the current organization's ID and excluding soft-deleted roles (deleted_at IS NULL).

For each active role, compute:
1. Role count: total number of active roles in the organization
2. Built-in vs custom breakdown: count of is_builtin = true vs false
3. Employee count per role: join with hrm_time_track_employees to count employees assigned to each role
4. Permission count per role: count entries in hrm_time_track_role_permissions for each role
5. Permission distribution: aggregate which permissions are most commonly assigned across roles

Return aggregated statistics including:
- Total role count
- Built-in role count and list
- Custom role count and list
- Employee distribution across roles
- Most common permissions
- Roles with highest employee counts

Ensure organization-scoped query using the authenticated user's current organization context. Do not include soft-deleted roles in the report.

responseBody.description: Role analytics report containing aggregated statistics about role distribution, permission assignments, and usage metrics within the organization.

operations.description:
Retrieves the effective permissions for the currently authenticated member within their selected organization context.

This endpoint returns the list of permission codes granted to the member through their assigned role. The permissions determine what actions the member can perform within the organization, including organization management, employee management, project management, time tracking, and reporting capabilities.

The effective permissions are calculated based on the member's employee record and the role assigned to that employee. If the member has no employee record in the organization or no role assigned, an empty permission list is returned.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve the current authenticated member's effective permissions from their role assignment.

1. Extract member_id from the authentication session token.
2. Extract organization_id from the organization context in the session.
3. Query hrm_time_track_employees to find the employee record matching member_id and organization_id.
4. If no employee record exists, return empty permissions array.
5. If employee has no role assigned (role_id is null), return empty permissions array.
6. Query hrm_time_track_role_permissions using the employee's role_id to get all permission codes.
7. Return the list of permission strings.

Error handling:
- If member_id is not found in session, return 401 Unauthorized.
- If organization_id is not found in session, return 400 Bad Request.
- If employee record is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), return empty permissions array.
- If role is soft-deleted, return empty permissions array.

responseBody.description: Array of permission codes representing the effective permissions granted to the current member through their role assignment.

authorizations.name: guest
authorizations.description: Unauthenticated visitors with limited access to public resources

authorizations.name: member
authorizations.description: Authenticated users who can belong to organizations and perform HRM and time tracking operations

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
