role.description:
The assigned role defining the employee's authority level within the project.

Allowed values are 'member' for standard access to view and contribute to the project, or 'project-lead' for elevated authority to manage tasks within the assigned project. This role-based control ensures appropriate task management permissions are granted.
role.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_project_members.role column. Allowed values: 'member' or 'project-lead'.

employee.description:
The employee assigned to this project.

This relation provides summary information about the employee including their identity (member), department, role, position, employment type, and status within the organization.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_project_members.employee via hrm_time_track_employee_id FK. Returns IHrmTimeTrackEmployee.ISummary to avoid circular references.

project.description:
The project to which the employee is assigned.

This relation provides summary information about the project including its name, description, color code, status, budget hours, and date range within the organization.
project.x-autobe-specification: Relation from hrm_time_track_project_members.project via hrm_time_track_project_id FK. Returns IHrmTimeTrackProject.ISummary to avoid circular references.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the project membership was created.

This field records when the employee was assigned to the project and is used for audit trails and tracking the history of project team composition.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_project_members.created_at. Auto-generated on record creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the project membership was last updated.

This field tracks when changes were made to the project member record, such as role modifications, and is automatically maintained by the system.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_project_members.updated_at. Auto-updated on record modification.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the project membership was soft deleted. Null indicates active membership.

This field enables soft deletion of project memberships, preserving historical data while removing the employee from active project access. When not null, the membership is considered terminated.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_project_members.deleted_at. Nullable DateTime for soft-delete support.

IHrmTimeTrackProjectMember.description:
Complete project member record representing an employee's assignment to a project.

This type includes all fields of the project member entity, including the assigned role that determines the employee's authority level within the project context. The role can be 'member' for standard access or 'project-lead' for elevated task management permissions.

Relations to employee and project are included as summary objects, providing essential context about the assigned employee and the project without including their full nested data structures.
IHrmTimeTrackProjectMember.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_project_members table. FK columns hrm_time_track_employee_id and hrm_time_track_project_id are transformed to relation objects (employee and project) using ISummary types to avoid circular references. Timestamps mapped directly. deleted_at is nullable for soft-delete support.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the timesheet-timelog association record.

This UUID identifies the specific link between a timelog and a timesheet in the approval workflow. Each association is unique and cannot be duplicated within the same timesheet.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs.id. Primary key uniquely identifying this timesheet-timelog association record.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this timelog was added to the timesheet.

This field tracks when the association was created, providing audit information about when timelogs were included in timesheets for approval processing. Useful for tracking timesheet assembly timelines.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs.created_at. Records when this timelog was added to the timesheet for approval processing.

timesheet.description:
The parent timesheet that includes this timelog for approval processing.

This relation provides the weekly approval context for the timelog, including the timesheet's status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected), week boundaries (Monday to Sunday), the employee who owns the timesheet, and the approver information when approved.
timesheet.x-autobe-specification: Relation via JOIN on hrm_time_track_timesheet_id to hrm_time_track_timesheets table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.ISummary with essential timesheet information (id, status, week dates, employee, approver, total_hours).

timelog.description:
The complete timelog entry included in this timesheet.

This relation contains the actual work time data: the date when work was performed, duration in seconds, billable status, optional task assignment, project association, employee who performed the work, and descriptive notes. This is the core time tracking information being submitted for approval.
timelog.x-autobe-specification: Relation via JOIN on hrm_time_track_timelog_id to hrm_time_track_timelogs table. Returns full IHrmTimeTrackTimelog entity with all its relations: employee (who performed the work), project (which project the time was logged against), task (optional specific task), and all timelog fields (date, duration_seconds, billable, notes).

IHrmTimeTrackTimesheetTimelog.description:
Timesheet-timelog association entity representing a single timelog entry included in a weekly timesheet for approval processing.

This entity links a timelog to a timesheet, establishing the relationship needed for the weekly approval workflow. The association includes metadata about when the timelog was added to the timesheet, along with complete timelog details including project and task information.

The timesheet relationship provides the approval context and week boundaries, while the timelog relationship contains the actual work time data (date, duration, billable status, notes).
IHrmTimeTrackTimesheetTimelog.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs table. Columns: id, created_at. Relations: timesheet via JOIN on hrm_time_track_timesheet_id to hrm_time_track_timesheets (returns .ISummary), timelog via JOIN on hrm_time_track_timelog_id to hrm_time_track_timelogs (returns full entity with its own relations: project, task, employee). FK columns (hrm_time_track_timesheet_id, hrm_time_track_timelog_id) are exposed as relation objects, not as scalar fields.

role.description:
Filter project members by their assigned role within the project.

Accepts 'member' for employees with standard access to view and contribute to the project, or 'project-lead' for employees with elevated authority to manage tasks within the project. This filter enables administrators to quickly identify team members with specific responsibility levels.
role.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter for exact match on hrm_time_track_project_members.role column. Allowed values: 'member' for standard project access, 'project-lead' for elevated task management authority. When provided, only project members with matching role are returned.

search.description:
Search for project members by employee name.

Performs a text search across employee name fields to find project members whose names match the search term. Supports partial matching, allowing users to find employees by entering fragments of their names. Useful for quickly locating specific team members in large project rosters.
search.x-autobe-specification: Text search parameter that performs case-insensitive search on employee name fields from hrm_time_track_employees table. The search is executed via JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id. Supports partial matching for finding employees by name fragments.

status.description:
Filter project members by their employment status.

Filters the project member list to show only employees with a specific employment status such as active, on leave, terminated, or pending. This helps administrators manage project teams by focusing on employees who are currently available or filtering out inactive personnel.
status.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter for exact match on hrm_time_track_employees.status column via JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id. Filters project members by their employment status (e.g., 'active', 'on leave', 'terminated', 'pending'). Only employees with matching status are included in results.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when the total number of project members exceeds the page limit. Page numbering starts from 1 (the first page). Use this parameter along with limit to navigate through large result sets efficiently.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter specifying the current page number to retrieve. 1-indexed (first page is 1, not 0). Defaults to 1 if not provided. Used with limit to control which subset of results is returned. Validates that page >= 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of project members to return per page.

Controls how many project member records are included in each page of results. Accepts values from 1 to 100. Larger values reduce the number of API calls needed but increase response size. Smaller values enable finer-grained pagination for better performance with large datasets.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter specifying the maximum number of records to return per page. Valid range is 1 to 100. Defaults to system default if not provided. Used with page to control result set size. Validates that 1 <= limit <= 100.

sort.description:
Field to sort the project member list by.

Determines which attribute is used to order the results. Options include sorting by role (member/project-lead), employee name (alphabetically), or assignment date (when the employee was added to the project). Combine with sortOrder to control ascending or descending order.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sorting parameter specifying which field to sort results by. Allowed values: 'role' (sort by project member role), 'employee_name' (sort by employee name from joined employees table), 'created_at' (sort by assignment date). Defaults to system default if not provided.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction for the project member list.

Controls whether results are ordered in ascending (A-Z, oldest-first) or descending (Z-A, newest-first) order. Works together with the sort parameter to fully define result ordering. For example, sorting by employee_name with asc gives alphabetical order, while desc gives reverse alphabetical order.
sortOrder.x-autobe-specification: Sorting parameter specifying the sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' for ascending order (A-Z, oldest-first), 'desc' for descending order (Z-A, newest-first). Defaults to 'asc' if not provided. Used in conjunction with sort parameter.

IHrmTimeTrackProjectMember.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating project members assigned to a project.

This DTO defines search criteria, pagination settings, and sorting preferences for retrieving project member lists. All fields are optional to allow flexible querying.

Filtering options include role-based filtering (member or project-lead), text search on employee names, and employee status filtering. Pagination controls the number of results returned per page and which page to retrieve. Sorting allows ordering results by role, employee name, or assignment date in ascending or descending order.
IHrmTimeTrackProjectMember.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Request parameters DTO for filtering and paginating project member lists. All properties are query parameters, not database columns.

Filtering:
- role: Exact match filter on hrm_time_track_project_members.role column (values: 'member' or 'project-lead')
- search: Text search on employee name fields from hrm_time_track_employees (via JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id)
- status: Filter on hrm_time_track_employees.status column (via JOIN)

Pagination:
- page: 1-indexed current page number, defaults to 1
- limit: Records per page, range 1-100, defaults to system limit

Sorting:
- sort: Field to sort by (role, employee_name, created_at)
- sortOrder: Sort direction (asc/desc), defaults to asc

All filters are optional and can be combined. The projectId path parameter filters hrm_time_track_project_id. Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL) are excluded from results.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the timesheet snapshot record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the snapshot, enabling precise identification and retrieval of individual status change events within the timesheet approval audit trail.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots.id. Primary key uniquely identifying this snapshot record.

timesheet.description:
The timesheet to which this snapshot belongs.

References the timesheet whose status change is captured in this snapshot. The timesheet summary includes week dates, approval status, total hours, and employee information, providing context for the status change event.
timesheet.x-autobe-specification: Relation via JOIN on hrm_time_track_timesheet_id to hrm_time_track_timesheets table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.ISummary with essential timesheet information.

member.description:
The member who performed the status change action.

References the user account that submitted, approved, or rejected the timesheet. The member summary includes identity information (email, name) for accountability and audit trail purposes.
member.x-autobe-specification: Relation via JOIN on hrm_time_track_member_id to hrm_time_track_members table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackMember.ISummary with member identity information.

status.description:
The timesheet status captured at the time of this snapshot.

Records the status value (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected) that the timesheet had when this snapshot was created. This denormalized field enables efficient querying of status history without joining to the timesheet table.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots.status. Records the timesheet status value at the time of this snapshot.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

Records the exact moment the status change occurred, providing precise timing information for audit purposes and compliance reporting. Used for sorting snapshots chronologically and calculating approval turnaround times.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots.created_at. Records the exact moment the status change occurred.

IHrmTimeTrackTimesheetSnapshot.description:
A timesheet snapshot capturing a point-in-time status change during the timesheet approval workflow.

This immutable audit record contains the timesheet status, the member who performed the action, and the exact timestamp of the status change. Snapshots provide compliance and accountability for timesheet status transitions including submission, approval, and rejection events. Organizations can use this data to review the complete approval history and verify who performed each action and when it occurred.
IHrmTimeTrackTimesheetSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots table. Fields: id (PK), status, created_at. Relations: timesheet via JOIN on hrm_time_track_timesheet_id to hrm_time_track_timesheets, member via JOIN on hrm_time_track_member_id to hrm_time_track_members. All fields are required and NOT NULL. FK columns are exposed as object references rather than raw IDs.

from_date.description:
Start date for filtering timelogs by date range.

Only timelogs with a date on or after this value will be included in the results. This parameter enables filtering timelogs within a specific time period for reporting and analysis purposes. The date comparison is timezone-aware and uses the organization's configured timezone.
from_date.x-autobe-specification: Lower bound date filter for timelog.date field. Filters timelogs where date >= from_date. Uses timezone-aware comparison based on organization timezone setting. Format: ISO 8601 datetime string.

to_date.description:
End date for filtering timelogs by date range.

Only timelogs with a date on or before this value will be included in the results. Combined with from_date, this parameter enables filtering timelogs within a specific time period for reporting and analysis purposes. The date comparison is timezone-aware and uses the organization's configured timezone.
to_date.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound date filter for timelog.date field. Filters timelogs where date <= to_date. Uses timezone-aware comparison based on organization timezone setting. Format: ISO 8601 datetime string.

project_id.description:
Project ID for filtering timelogs by project.

Only timelogs associated with the specified project will be included in the results. This enables viewing all time logged against a particular project for project-specific reporting and time tracking analysis. The project must belong to the user's current organization context.
project_id.x-autobe-specification: Filter timelogs by project ID. Filters on hrm_time_track_timelogs.hrm_time_track_project_id field. Only timelogs associated with the specified project will be returned. Format: UUID string.

task_id.description:
Task ID for filtering timelogs by task.

Only timelogs associated with the specified task will be included in the results. This enables viewing all time logged against a particular task for detailed task-level time tracking and analysis. The task must belong to the user's current organization context. Note that timelogs can exist without task assignment (project-level timelogs).
task_id.x-autobe-specification: Filter timelogs by task ID. Filters on hrm_time_track_timelogs.hrm_time_track_task_id field. Only timelogs associated with the specified task will be returned. Format: UUID string. Note: task_id is nullable in the database, so timelogs without task assignment will not match this filter.

employee_id.description:
Employee ID for filtering timelogs by employee.

Only timelogs created by the specified employee will be included in the results. This enables viewing time entries for specific team members for management and reporting purposes. Users without time management permissions can only filter by their own employee ID. Users with time management permission can filter by any employee within the organization.
employee_id.x-autobe-specification: Filter timelogs by employee ID. Filters on hrm_time_track_timelogs.hrm_time_track_employee_id field. Only timelogs created by the specified employee will be returned. Format: UUID string. Authorization: Users without time management permission can only filter by their own employee_id.

billable.description:
Billable status filter for timelogs.

When set to true, only billable timelogs (chargeable to clients) are included in the results. When set to false, only non-billable timelogs (internal work) are included. If not provided, both billable and non-billable timelogs are returned. This enables separating chargeable work from internal activities for billing and reporting purposes.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Filter timelogs by billable status. Filters on hrm_time_track_timelogs.billable boolean field. When true, only billable timelogs are returned. When false, only non-billable timelogs are returned. If not provided, both billable and non-billable timelogs are included.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when the total number of timelogs exceeds the page limit. Page numbering starts from 1 (not 0). Defaults to page 1 if not provided. The response includes pagination metadata showing the current page, total pages, and total record count.
page.x-autobe-specification: Page number for pagination (1-indexed). Defaults to 1 if not provided. Used to retrieve specific pages of results when the total number of timelogs exceeds the limit. Minimum value is 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of timelog records per page.

Controls how many timelog entries are returned in each page of paginated results. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100. Defaults to 20 records per page if not provided. Larger limits reduce the number of API calls needed but increase response size.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page. Defaults to 20 if not provided. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100. Controls how many timelog records are returned in each page of results.

sort.description:
Field name for sorting timelog results.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the timelog results. Supported sort fields include date, duration_seconds, project_id, employee_id, and id. Defaults to sorting by date if not provided. Combined with the order parameter to control ascending or descending sort direction.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Field name to sort results by. Supported fields: date, duration_seconds, project_id, employee_id, id. Defaults to 'date' if not provided. The field must exist in hrm_time_track_timelogs table.

order.description:
Sort direction for timelog results.

Specifies whether to sort results in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order. Defaults to descending order if not provided. Combined with the sort parameter to control how timelogs are ordered. For example, sort=date with order=desc shows newest timelogs first.
order.x-autobe-specification: Sort direction for results. Allowed values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'desc' if not provided. Applied to the field specified in the sort parameter.

IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for listing timelogs with filtering, pagination, and sorting capabilities.

This request object allows filtering timelogs by date range, project, task, employee, and billable status. Pagination parameters control the number of results returned, while sorting options determine the order of results.

All fields are optional. When no filters are provided, all timelogs within the user's organization context are returned. Timelogs are strictly isolated per organization - users only see timelogs within their current organization context based on their authentication token.
IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Request DTO for timelog listing/search operation at PATCH /hrmTimeTrack/member/timelogs. All fields are optional query parameters used for filtering and pagination.

Filtering logic:
- from_date and to_date: Filter on hrm_time_track_timelogs.date field using range comparison (date >= from_date AND date <= to_date)
- project_id: Filter on hrm_time_track_timelogs.hrm_time_track_project_id field
- task_id: Filter on hrm_time_track_timelogs.hrm_time_track_task_id field
- employee_id: Filter on hrm_time_track_timelogs.hrm_time_track_employee_id field
- billable: Filter on hrm_time_track_timelogs.billable boolean field

Pagination:
- page: Current page number (1-indexed), defaults to 1
- limit: Maximum records per page, defaults to 20, max 100

Sorting:
- sort: Field name to sort by (date, duration_seconds, project_id, employee_id, etc.)
- order: Sort direction (asc or desc), defaults to desc

Authorization:
- Organization context from JWT token (hrm_time_track_organization_id filter applied automatically)
- Employee visibility based on permissions (own timelogs only vs all organization timelogs)

Query always excludes soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL) unless explicitly requested.

status.description:
Current approval workflow status of the timesheet.

Allowed values are 'draft' (editable by employee), 'submitted' (locked, awaiting approval), 'approved' (immutable, official record), or 'rejected' (returned to draft with rejection reason). This field controls the workflow transition and must follow valid status transition rules. The backend validates that the requested transition is permitted based on current status and user permissions.
status.x-autobe-specification: Maps to timesheet status transitions. Allowed values: 'draft', 'submitted', 'approved', 'rejected'. Backend validates: (1) timesheet exists, (2) user has permission, (3) status transition is valid per workflow rules (draft→submitted, submitted→approved/rejected, rejected→draft, approved→locked). Server automatically sets approved_at/rejected_at timestamps and hrm_time_track_member_id approver reference based on transition.

rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Maps to timesheet rejection_reason column. Required when status transitions to 'rejected'. Must be non-empty string providing reason for rejection to inform employee of issues to address. Backend validates rejection_reason is provided and not empty when status is 'rejected'. Field is nullable in database for timesheets not in rejected state.
rejection_reason.description:
Reason provided by the approver when rejecting a timesheet.

This field is required when rejecting a submitted timesheet and must contain a non-empty explanation of issues to address. The reason is recorded for the employee to review and address before resubmission. This field is optional for other status transitions (draft, submitted, approved) and will be null for timesheets not in rejected state.

IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying a timesheet's status in the approval workflow.

This DTO supports timesheet status transitions including submitting draft timesheets for approval, approving or rejecting submitted timesheets, and returning rejected timesheets to draft status. The status field controls the workflow transition, and rejection_reason must be provided when rejecting a timesheet to inform the employee of issues to address.
IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Maps status field to timesheet status transitions. rejection_reason required when status transitions to 'rejected'. Backend validates: (1) timesheet exists, (2) user has permission, (3) status transition is valid per workflow rules, (4) rejection_reason provided when rejecting. Server automatically sets approved_at/rejected_at timestamps and hrm_time_track_member_id approver reference.

IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.IUpdate.description:
Update request for modifying an existing timelog record.

This DTO allows modification of timelog details including work date, duration, project assignment, optional task assignment, billable status, and descriptive notes. All fields are optional to support partial updates.
IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Maps to hrm_time_track_timelogs table update operation. Allowed fields: date, duration_seconds, hrm_time_track_project_id, hrm_time_track_task_id, billable, notes. Excluded: id (auto-generated), hrm_time_track_employee_id (ownership immutable), hrm_time_track_organization_id (context from JWT), created_at/deleted_at (system-managed). All properties optional for partial updates. Backend validates: timelog exists, ownership or permission, project is active if changed, task belongs to project if both changed.

IHrmTimeTrackTask.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new task within a project.

Tasks represent discrete units of work that can be assigned to employees, organized with parent-child hierarchy, and tracked through status transitions. Each task must belong to a project and can include priority levels, effort estimates, and optional employee assignment.

Required fields are project reference and task title. Optional fields include employee assignee, parent task for subtask organization, description, priority classification, workflow status, and effort estimation.
IHrmTimeTrackTask.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to hrm_time_track_tasks table. Required: hrm_time_track_project_id (FK to hrm_time_track_projects), title. Optional: hrm_time_track_employee_id (FK to hrm_time_track_employees, nullable), parent_task_id (self-reference FK, nullable), description (nullable), priority (String, defaults to 'medium'), status (String, defaults to 'open'), effort_estimate (Float, nullable). Excluded: id (UUID auto-generated), created_at/updated_at (auto timestamps), deleted_at (soft delete managed by system), effort_actual (populated via updates only).

id.description:
Unique identifier for this task status history entry.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the task history record, allowing precise identification and retrieval of individual status change events. The identifier is generated upon creation and never changes, ensuring stable references for audit trail purposes.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_task_histories.id. Primary key uniquely identifying this task history entry. Generated UUID, immutable after creation.

previous_status.description:
The task status before the change occurred.

This field captures the previous state of the task prior to the status transition, enabling tracking of how tasks progress through their lifecycle. Combined with new_status, it provides a complete picture of the status change event for audit and compliance purposes.
previous_status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_task_histories.previous_status. Stores the task status value before the status change occurred. NOT NULL, immutable after creation. Valid values conform to Task Status Classification business category.

new_status.description:
The new task status after the change.

This field records the resulting state of the task following the status transition. It represents the task's current status at the time this history entry was created, providing the endpoint of the status change event for audit trail reconstruction.
new_status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_task_histories.new_status. Stores the task status value after the status change occurred. NOT NULL, immutable after creation. Valid values conform to Task Status Classification business category.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the status change occurred.

This field records the precise date and time when the task status transition took place, enabling chronological tracking of task progression. The timestamp is captured at the moment of status change and never modified, ensuring accurate audit trail timing for compliance and reporting purposes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_task_histories.created_at. Records the exact timestamp when the status change occurred. NOT NULL, immutable after creation. Stored as UTC datetime with timezone information.

task.description:
The task whose status changed.

This field provides a reference to the task that underwent the status transition, including essential task information such as title, project assignment, and current status. The task relationship enables users to understand which specific work item was affected by the status change recorded in this history entry.
task.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping via JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id to hrm_time_track_tasks table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackTask.ISummary object. NOT NULL - every history entry must reference a valid task. FK column hrm_time_track_task_id is exposed through this relation object, not as a separate scalar field.

member.description:
The member who performed the status change.

This field identifies the user account responsible for making the task status transition, providing accountability and audit trail information. The member relationship includes user identity details such as email and name, enabling tracking of who modified task statuses for compliance and workflow analysis purposes.
member.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping via JOIN on hrm_time_track_member_id to hrm_time_track_members table. Returns IHrmTimeTrackMember.ISummary object. NOT NULL - every history entry must reference a valid member who made the change. FK column hrm_time_track_member_id is exposed through this relation object, not as a separate scalar field.

IHrmTimeTrackTaskHistory.description:
Complete task status history entry recording an immutable audit record of a task status change.

This type represents a single status transition event for a task, capturing the previous status, new status, exact timestamp of the change, and the member who performed the status transition. Task history entries are append-only and cannot be modified or deleted after creation, ensuring an accurate permanent audit trail for compliance and tracking purposes.

The entry includes references to both the task that changed status and the member who made the change, providing complete context for understanding how tasks progress through their lifecycle stages.
IHrmTimeTrackTaskHistory.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_task_histories table. Columns: id, previous_status, new_status, created_at. Relations: task via JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id to hrm_time_track_tasks, member via JOIN on hrm_time_track_member_id to hrm_time_track_members. All fields are NOT NULL and immutable after creation. Task history entries are append-only audit records that cannot be modified or deleted.

IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.description:
Complete timesheet entity representing a weekly time tracking collection for employee approval workflow.

A timesheet groups an employee's timelogs into a weekly period (Monday to Sunday) for submission and approval. The timesheet follows a four-state approval workflow: draft (editable by employee), submitted (locked, awaiting approval), approved (immutable, official record), and rejected (returned to draft with rejection reason).

The response includes the timesheet's week dates, current approval status, approval metadata (approver, approval timestamp, rejection reason), and all associated timelogs. Employee information is included as a reference to the timesheet owner.
IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timesheets table. JOIN hrm_time_track_employees on hrm_time_track_employee_id for employee details. LEFT JOIN hrm_time_track_members on hrm_time_track_member_id for approver (nullable). JOIN hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs junction table then hrm_time_track_timelogs for timelogs array. Filter deleted_at IS NULL.

add.description:
Array of timelog UUIDs to add to the timesheet.

Each UUID in this array represents a timelog that will be associated with the specified timesheet. The backend validates that each timelog exists, belongs to the same employee as the timesheet, and has a date within the timesheet's week range. Duplicate associations are skipped without error.
add.x-autobe-specification: Array of timelog UUIDs to associate with the timesheet. Each UUID is validated against hrm_time_track_timelogs table: timelog must exist and not be soft-deleted, must belong to same employee as the timesheet (hrm_time_track_employee_id match), timelog date must fall within timesheet week range (week_start_date to week_end_date). For each valid UUID, a new record is created in hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs junction table linking the timesheet to the timelog. Duplicate associations (timelog already in timesheet) are skipped without error.

remove.description:
Array of timelog UUIDs to remove from the timesheet.

Each UUID in this array represents a timelog that will be disassociated from the specified timesheet. The backend validates that each association exists before deletion. This operation only removes the timelog from the timesheet collection; the timelog itself remains in the system and can be added to other timesheets.

Each UUID is validated against hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs junction table: the association record must exist between the timesheet and timelog. For each valid UUID, the association record is deleted from the junction table. This does not delete the timelog itself, only removes it from the timesheet's collection.

IHrmTimeTrackTimesheet.ITimelogUpdate.description:
Request body for updating timelog associations on a timesheet.

This object contains arrays of timelog identifiers to add to or remove from the specified timesheet. Use the add array to include new timelogs in the timesheet, and the remove array to exclude existing timelogs. Both arrays are optional, allowing you to perform add-only or remove-only operations. The timesheet must be in draft status for modifications to be accepted.

The add array contains timelog UUIDs to associate with the timesheet (creates records in hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs junction table). The remove array contains timelog UUIDs to disassociate (deletes records from junction table). Backend validates: timesheet exists and is not soft-deleted, timesheet status is 'draft', authenticated employee owns the timesheet, each timelog exists and belongs to same employee, each timelog date falls within timesheet week range, and association already exists for remove operations. Both arrays are optional for add-only or remove-only operations.

IHrmTimeTrackTask.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing task's attributes including title, description, status, priority, effort estimates, employee assignment, and parent task relationship.

This DTO allows modification of task properties while preserving structural integrity. The task's project assignment cannot be changed after creation. Status transitions are validated and recorded in task history. Employee reassignment requires the target employee to be a member of the same project. Parent task assignment enables one-level subtask nesting only.

Excludes: id, hrm_time_track_project_id (immutable), timestamps. Status changes trigger task history recording.

search.description:
Search query for finding task history records by status values.

previous_status.description:

new_status.description:

End date for filtering history records by creation timestamp.

to_date.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound filter on hrm_time_track_task_histories.created_at column. Uses less-than-or-equal comparison (<=). Filters history entries created on or before this timestamp.

member_id.description:

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Page numbering starts from 1. Combined with limit to control the number of records returned per page. Useful for browsing through large result sets.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination page number (1-indexed). Used with limit to calculate OFFSET in SQL query: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Minimum value is 1. Defaults to 1 if not provided.

limit.description:

Controls how many history records are included in each page of results. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100. Combined with page parameter for pagination. Larger values return more data per request but may impact performance.

IHrmTimeTrackTaskHistory.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating task status history records.

Use these parameters to search, filter, and paginate through task status change history. All fields are optional and can be combined for complex queries.

The search parameter performs text matching across status fields. The previous_status and new_status parameters allow exact filtering on specific status values. The from_date and to_date parameters define a date range for history entries. The member_id parameter filters by the user who made status changes. The page and limit parameters control pagination of results.

Request DTO for filtering and paginating task status history records in list operations. This schema defines query parameters for the PATCH /hrmTimeTrack/member/tasks/{taskId}/histories endpoint.

Filter mappings:
- search: Text search across previous_status and new_status columns using ILIKE or trigram similarity
- previous_status: Exact equality filter on hrm_time_track_task_histories.previous_status column
- new_status: Exact equality filter on hrm_time_track_task_histories.new_status column
- from_date: Lower bound filter on hrm_time_track_task_histories.created_at column (>=)
- to_date: Upper bound filter on hrm_time_track_task_histories.created_at column (<=)

- limit: Maximum records per page, combined with page for LIMIT/OFFSET pagination

The taskId filter is obtained from the path parameter, not this request body.

cursor.description:

IHrmTimeTrackTimerSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for filtering timer snapshots including event type, date ranges, and pagination parameters.

This request object supports querying timer snapshots with flexible filtering options. Timer snapshots capture the complete audit trail of timer lifecycle events including start, stop, discard, and edit operations.

Filtering is supported by event type to retrieve specific snapshot categories, and by date range to narrow results to a specific time period. Pagination parameters control the number of results returned and the page offset. Sorting parameters allow ordering results by various fields.

description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.description. Optional description of work being performed during timer session. Nullable in database - employees may not provide a description.
description.description:
Optional description of the work being performed during this timer session.

Employees can use this field to note what specific work is being done, providing context for the time being tracked. This description can be edited while the timer is running, allowing corrections and updates to work context without stopping the timer session. Null when no description is provided.

IHrmTimeTrackTimer.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a timer session for list displays, including essential timer information and related entity references.

This summary includes the timer's core identification and status information along with references to the associated employee, project, and optional task. It is optimized for list views and search results where full timer details are not needed.

The timer represents an active time tracking session that records work time in real-time. Each employee can have at most one active timer at any time.

Relations: employee via JOIN (required), project via JOIN (required), task via JOIN (nullable). Excluded: updated_at (not essential for summary), foreign key IDs (converted to object references).

id.description:
Unique identifier for the timer snapshot record.

This UUID identifies a specific point-in-time capture of a timer's state during its lifecycle event.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.id. Primary key uniquely identifying each timer snapshot record.

event_type.description:
Type of timer event that triggered this snapshot.

Allowed values:
- 'start': Timer began tracking time
- 'stop': Timer completed and recorded duration
- 'discard': Timer was cancelled without recording time
- 'edit': Timer attributes were modified after creation
event_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.event_type. Allowed values: 'start', 'stop', 'discard', 'edit'. Indicates the type of timer lifecycle event that triggered this snapshot.

duration_seconds.description:
Duration in seconds recorded at the time of this snapshot event.

For 'start' events, this value is 0. For 'stop' events, this contains the total tracked duration. For 'discard' events, this may contain partial duration or 0. For 'edit' events, this reflects the modified duration.
duration_seconds.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.duration_seconds. Integer value representing the duration in seconds recorded at the time of the snapshot event.

started_at.description:
Timestamp when the timer was originally started.

started_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.started_at. Timestamp when the timer was originally started. This field remains constant across all snapshots for the same timer.

note.description:

created_at.description:

created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.created_at. Timestamp when this snapshot record was created, indicating when the timer event occurred.

employee.description:

project.description:
The project this timer is tracking time against.

creator.description:
The member who created this snapshot event.

IHrmTimeTrackTimerSnapshot.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a timer snapshot capturing a specific event in a timer's lifecycle.

Timer snapshots provide an immutable audit trail of timer sessions, recording the state at key moments: when a timer starts tracking time, when attributes are edited, when it stops and records duration, or when it is discarded. Each snapshot includes the event type, duration, timestamps, and references to the associated employee, project, optional task, and the member who created the snapshot.

This summary type is optimized for list displays, including essential identification and event details while excluding verbose content.
IHrmTimeTrackTimerSnapshot.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots table. This ISummary provides a lightweight representation of timer lifecycle events for list displays. All scalar fields are denormalized from the snapshot table for audit trail integrity. Relations are exposed as ISummary objects: employee (hrm_time_track_employees), project (hrm_time_track_projects), task (hrm_time_track_tasks, nullable), and creator/member (hrm_time_track_members). The timer relation and all FK columns are excluded as they are not needed for summary list views when relations are present.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the timelog entry.

date.description:
Date when the work was performed.

This field represents the calendar date of the work activity. Timelogs can be filtered by date range to view entries within specific periods. The date is stored as a datetime value for precise time tracking and reporting.

Duration of the work in seconds.

duration_seconds.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timelogs.duration_seconds. Integer field storing duration in seconds for precision and ease of calculation.

Whether this time entry is billable to a client.

Billable status separates chargeable work from internal or non-billable activities. Timelogs can be filtered by billable status for billing and reporting purposes. This field is essential for financial tracking and client invoicing.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timelogs.billable. Boolean field indicating whether the time entry is billable to a client.

notes.description:

IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.description:
Complete timelog record representing a single time entry for work performed by an employee.

This entity includes all timelog details: the work date, duration in seconds, project assignment, optional task assignment, billable status, and descriptive notes. It also includes the associated employee who performed the work, the project the time was logged against, and optionally the specific task if time was tracked at task level.

Timelogs are organization-scoped and form the foundation for timesheet creation and approval workflows. Each timelog is owned by the employee who creates it and cannot be transferred to another employee. Timelogs can be filtered by date range, project, task, and billable status for reporting purposes.

Relations: employee (JOIN on hrm_time_track_employee_id to hrm_time_track_employees), project (JOIN on hrm_time_track_project_id to hrm_time_track_projects), task (LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id to hrm_time_track_tasks, nullable). Organization context is derived from JWT authentication, not exposed in response. Timesheets relation is excluded as it's an aggregation relation accessed through separate endpoint. All scalar fields are directly mapped. Timestamps include created_at, updated_at, and nullable deleted_at for soft delete visibility.

task_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.hrm_time_track_task_id. Optional task association for granular time tracking. Nullable in database, exposed as optional in Create DTO.

Optional task ID for granular time tracking within the project.

This field allows employees to associate the timer with a specific task within the selected project. Task association is optional - if not provided, the time will be tracked at the project level only. If specified, the task must belong to the project referenced in project_id.

description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timers.description. Optional work description field. Nullable in database, exposed as optional in Create DTO.
description.description:
Optional description of the work being performed during this timer session.

Employees can use this field to document what specific work is being tracked. This description provides context for the time entry and can be edited while the timer is running. If not provided, the timer will have no description.

IHrmTimeTrackTimer.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new timer session.

This object contains the configuration for starting a live time tracking session. The project association is required to establish which project the time will be tracked against. Task association is optional for more granular tracking at the task level within the project. A description can be provided to document the specific work being performed.

The employee context is automatically derived from the authenticated session, and the start timestamp is set automatically when the timer begins.
IHrmTimeTrackTimer.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: project_id -> hrm_time_track_project_id (required), task_id -> hrm_time_track_task_id (optional), description -> description (optional). Excluded: id (auto-generated), started_at (auto-set to DateTime.now()), is_active (auto-set to true), created_at/updated_at (auto-managed), hrm_time_track_employee_id (from JWT session context).

IHrmTimeTrackTask.description:
Complete task entity with all attributes and related entities.

This type represents a full task detail including the task's core attributes (title, description, priority, status, effort estimates), timestamps, and all related entities. The project field provides the parent project context, the employee field shows the assigned worker (if any), and the parentTask field indicates if this is a subtask. The subtasks array contains child tasks (one-level nesting only), and taskHistories provides the audit trail of status changes.

The following fields may be null: description (optional task details), employee (unassigned tasks), parentTask (top-level tasks), effort_estimate and effort_actual (optional time tracking), deleted_at (active tasks).
IHrmTimeTrackTask.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_tasks table. Relations: project via JOIN with hrm_time_track_projects (required), employee via JOIN with hrm_time_track_employees (nullable), parentTask via self-referencing JOIN (nullable), subtasks via query where parent_task_id = task.id, taskHistories via query from hrm_time_track_task_histories where task_id = task.id. All relations use ISummary to prevent circular references and reduce payload size.

status.description:
Optional filter to narrow results to snapshots with a specific approval workflow status.

When provided, only snapshots matching the specified status value are returned. Valid status values correspond to the timesheet approval workflow states: draft, submitted, approved, or rejected. This enables clients to view only snapshots of a particular type, such as all approval events or all rejection events.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot records to return per page.

Controls the size of each page in the paginated results. This parameter determines how many snapshots are included in a single response. The value must be between 1 and 100. Combined with the page parameter, it enables clients to navigate through large result sets efficiently.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Computed pagination parameter controlling maximum records per page. Applied as LIMIT clause in SQL query. Minimum value is 1, maximum value is 100. Default value typically 20 or similar. Used with page to calculate offset.

cursor.description:
Cursor token for cursor-based pagination.

An opaque string token that represents a position in the result set. Used for cursor-based pagination as an alternative to offset-based pagination. The cursor is obtained from the previous page response and enables efficient navigation through large datasets without the performance issues of deep offset queries.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Computed parameter for cursor-based pagination. Contains an opaque cursor string from the previous page response. Used to retrieve the next page of results without using page/limit. Mutually exclusive with page-based pagination.

IHrmTimeTrackActivityLog.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for listing and searching activity logs with filtering, sorting, and pagination support.

This request body allows filtering activity logs by date range, activity type, and associated entities. All fields are optional, enabling flexible query combinations. Results are automatically scoped to the authenticated member's organizations.

### Filtering Options

- **search**: Text search across activity descriptions
- **activity_type**: Filter by specific activity type (e.g., employee_created, project_archived, task_status_changed)
- **from_date/to_date**: Date range filter for created_at timestamp
- **entity filters**: Filter by associated employee, project, task, timesheet, role, contract, or department

### Pagination

- **page**: Page number (default: 1, minimum: 1)
- **limit**: Results per page (default: 20, minimum: 1, maximum: 100)
IHrmTimeTrackActivityLog.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Request DTO for activity log listing endpoint with filtering and pagination support. This schema defines query parameters for searching and filtering hrm_time_track_activity_logs records.

**Filtering Logic:**
- search: Performs LIKE query on description column for text matching
- activity_type: Exact match filter on activity_type column
- from_date/to_date: Range filter on created_at column (>= from_date AND <= to_date)
- employee_id: Filter by hrm_time_track_employee_id foreign key column
- project_id: Filter by hrm_time_track_project_id foreign key column
- task_id: Filter by hrm_time_track_task_id foreign key column
- timesheet_id: Filter by hrm_time_track_timesheet_id foreign key column
- role_id: Filter by hrm_time_track_role_id foreign key column
- employee_contract_id: Filter by hrm_time_track_employee_contract_id foreign key column
- department_id: Filter by hrm_time_track_department_id foreign key column

**Pagination:**
- page: Page number (1-indexed, default: 1, minimum: 1)
- limit: Records per page (default: 20, minimum: 1, maximum: 100)

**Multi-tenancy:**
- Results automatically scoped to requesting member's organizations via JWT context
- No organization_id in request body - derived from authenticated user's session

**Sorting:**
- Default order by created_at DESC (newest first)

**Query Construction:**
All filter fields are optional. Query builds dynamic WHERE clause based on provided parameters. Empty search returns all activity logs for the user's organizations.

project.description:
The project the timer session is associated with.

project.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.project relation. JOIN on hrm_time_track_project_id to hrm_time_track_projects.id. Returns IHrmTimeTrackProject.ISummary object with project identification and status. Denormalized for audit trail integrity.

task.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.task relation. LEFT JOIN on hrm_time_track_task_id to hrm_time_track_tasks.id. member.description:

member.x-autobe-specification: Relation mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots.member relation (created_by FK). JOIN on created_by to hrm_time_track_members.id. IHrmTimeTrackTimerSnapshot.description:
Timer snapshot record capturing the state of a timer at a specific lifecycle event.

Timer snapshots are immutable audit trail records that preserve the complete state of a timer session at moments when significant events occur: when a timer starts, stops, is discarded, or is edited. Each snapshot contains denormalized data including the employee, project, task associations, duration, timestamps, and work description, ensuring the audit trail remains accurate even if related records are modified or deleted.

The event_type field indicates which lifecycle event triggered the snapshot (start, stop, discard, or edit). Duration is stored in seconds, and timestamps are in ISO 8601 format. The note field provides optional context about the work being tracked.
IHrmTimeTrackTimerSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots table. All scalar columns (id, event_type, duration_seconds, started_at, stopped_at, note, created_at) mapped directly. Foreign key columns converted to relation objects: hrm_time_track_timer_id → timer (IHrmTimeTrackTimer.ISummary), hrm_time_track_employee_id → employee (IHrmTimeTrackEmployee.ISummary), hrm_time_track_project_id → project (IHrmTimeTrackProject.ISummary), hrm_time_track_task_id → task (IHrmTimeTrackTask.ISummary, nullable), created_by → member (IHrmTimeTrackMember.ISummary). Query uses JOINs to fetch related entity data. This is a Read DTO returning complete snapshot with all denormalized relationship data for immutable audit trail.

Summary representation of a timelog entry for list displays, including project, task, and employee information.

IHrmTimeTrackTimelog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_time_track_timelogs table for scalar fields (id, date, duration_seconds, billable, notes, created_at, updated_at).
